newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania takes in 91 percent of its 1997 wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Romania takes in 91 percent of its 1997 wheat crop.

text.p: Romania has almost completed wheat harvesting and data show bad weather in recent weeks damaged at least 200,000 hectares under the crop, the Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday.
A ministry statement said data collected up to Monday showed harvesting had been completed on 2.19 million ha, or 91 percent of the 2.38 million under wheat.
Farmers had taken in 6.66 million tonnes of wheat so far, with the average yield amounting to 3,026 kg per ha, slightly higher than initial estimates of 2,963 kg, it said.
Ministry estimates put the 1997 wheat crop at 6.9 million tonnes, compared with 3.1 million last year.

Heavy rains and floods during harvesting had seriously damaged the wheat crop, reports in the local media said. They said the quality of the wheat --- especially in unharvested areas as well as in silos -- had reportedly been affected by humidity.
Ministry officials said they still have to gather data from across the country in order to make a final assessment.
"At this stage it is impossible to have a clear picture," one said.

Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu last week said losses amounted to some 900,000 tonnes of wheat, which had germinated due to the humidity. But the losses would be recouped by exporting that wheat to Middle East countries, he said.
He also said Romania's plans to export a surplus of two million tonnes of wheat remained unaltered.
